zh: 后来，在西方许多圈子里，雅尔塔成了西方天真地把东欧交给斯大林的象征。这是极大的过度简化。尽管战时人民阵线在西方引起了相当天真地信任斯大林民主意图的情绪，波兰的命运实际上是由西方盟国无法控制的军事因素决定的。盟国从斯大林那里争取到所能得到的有限让步，抱着他或许真会遵守承诺的渺茫希望。的确，正是这些纸面承诺的存在，后来使西方得以论证苏联在东欧的存在不合法。
en: Later, in many quarters in the West, Yalta became the symbol of the West’s naive surrender of Eastern Europe to Stalin. This is a great oversimplification. Although the wartime Popular Front had engendered in the West considerable naive trust in Stalin’s democratic intentions, Poland’s fate was in fact decided by military factors over which the Western Allies had no control. The Allies got what few concessions they could from Stalin in the low-odds hope that he might actually keep his promises. Indeed, the fact that these paper promises existed later made it possible for the West to argue the illegitimacy of the Soviet presence in Eastern Europe.

zh: 承诺未被履行，源于一个简单事实：斯大林自1939年以来一贯如此，不信任任何他不能直接控制的政治安排，这使苏联对波兰事务的干预不可避免。因为波兰扼守从柏林通往莫斯科的入侵通道，地缘政治上太重要，其地位不能听凭偶然。然而，任何从雅尔塔同意的自由选举中产生的波兰政府都会是反苏的；即便它接受适用于芬兰的那种强加联盟，也仍不会是苏联安全体系中万无一失的一环。因此斯大林绝不满足于一个不由共产党人控制的波兰政府，而他通过操纵1947年选举实现了这一点。甚至他给波兰人的重大补偿礼物，也是一种把他们永久绑在俄国身上的手段；因为把前德国省份并入波兰，并得到英美赞同，意味着此后波兰将永远需要与俄国结盟以对抗可能的德国复仇主义。于是在1939至1947年间，在关键的波兰案例中，未来苏维埃帝国的公式被制定出来。而这个关键案例也产生了使大同盟瓦解为冷战的各种利益冲突和相互猜疑。
en: That the promises were not kept derived from the simple fact that Stalin, true to his form since 1939, would not trust any political arrangement that he did not control directly, and this made Soviet intervention in Polish affairs inevitable. For Poland, astride the invasion corridor from Berlin to Moscow, was too important geopolitically for its status to be left to chance. Yet any Polish government that would emerge from the free elections agreed to at Yalta would be anti-Soviet; and even if it accepted the kind of imposed alliance that applied to Finland, it would still not be a foolproof element in the Soviet security system. So Stalin would settle for nothing less than a Polish government controlled by Communists, and this he achieved by rigging the election of 1947. Even his great compensatory gift to the Poles was a means of tying them permanently to Russia; for the incorporation into Poland of the former German provinces, with the approval of Britain and America, meant that henceforth Poland would always need a Russian alliance against possible German revanchism. Thus, between 1939 and 1947, in the crucial Polish case, the formula for the future Soviet empire was worked out. And this same crucial case also generated the conflicts of interest and the mutual suspicions that dissolved the Grand Alliance into the Cold War.

zh: 1945年斯大林打算走多远？苏联在东欧的扩张主义是冷战的根本原因吗？还是说，如果西方对他的恐惧以更多理解回应，他的胃口以及因此而来的国际紧张本可以得到节制？对这些问题的回答，从丘吉尔1946年“铁幕”演说中惊慌的诊断——苏联的侵略性是天生的——到所罗门式地把同等责任归于东西方，再到扭曲的“修正主义”论点，说斯大林只是在抵御美国的核讹诈。冷战进行期间，这些不同立场不只是历史解释的变体；它们也是对苏联加强或减弱军事准备和外交坚定的论证。既然冷战已经结束，这些辩论的政治激情已经消退，对史实作更切合实际的评估应当是可能的。
en: How far did Stalin intend to go in 1945? And was Soviet expansionism in Eastern Europe the root cause of the Cold War? Or could his appetites, and therefore international tensions, have been moderated by a more understanding response to his fears on the part of the West? Answers to these questions have ranged from Churchill’s alarmed diagnosis in his “iron curtain” speech of 1946 that Soviet aggressiveness was innate, to a Solomonic attribution of equal blame to East and West, to contorted “revisionist” arguments that Stalin was simply defending himself against American nuclear blackmail. While the Cold War was on, these various positions were not just varieties of historical interpretation; they were also arguments for greater or lesser military preparedness and diplomatic firmness towards the Soviet Union. Now that the Cold War is over, the political passion has gone out of these debates and a more realistic assessment of the record ought to be possible.

zh: 简言之，在冷战酝酿的关键年份1946—1948年，斯大林并不知道自己会走多远。但他最终走得那么远并非偶然，而一旦他到达著名的铁幕线，一个持久的冷对抗时期就不可避免。
换句话说，冷战的基本原因不在于任何一方的错误或误解，而在于一个说来平淡无奇的事实：共产主义政体与宪政民主政体之间的结构性不相容。鉴于苏联的存在本身，冷战是不可避免的，因此当苏联崩溃时它也就自动结束。同样，冷战年代的紧张并非源于某种根深蒂固的俄国扩张主义，因为俄国仍然存在，却在收缩。冷战毋宁源于苏联特有的社会主义权力组织方法，以及把这些方法推向国际舞台。
en: Briefly, in the crucial years of the Cold War’s gestation, 1946-1948, Stalin did not know how far he was going to go. But it was no accident that he eventually went as far as he did, and once he had reached the famous line of the iron curtain, an enduring period of cold hostilities was inevitable.

In other words, the basic cause of the Cold War lay not in any mistakes or misunderstandings on either side, but, quite tritely, in the structural incompatibility between Communist and constitutional democratic polities. The Cold War was inevitable given the simple existence of the Soviet Union, and it therefore automatically ended when the Soviet Union collapsed. By the same token, the tension of the Cold War years did not derive from some inveterate Russian expansionism, for Russia is still there but is contracting. Rather, the Cold War derived from specifically Soviet socialist methods of organizing power and the projection of these methods into the international arena.

zh: 话虽如此，还必须补充：1946—1948年间，西方遏制苏联扩张的努力加速并强化了这种扩张。局势的基本事实是苏联征服了直到易北河和亚得里亚海的大陆大部分。这部分是希特勒失败不可避免的结果，部分是苏联有意推行的政策的产物。早在1940年，斯大林就因巴尔干问题与希特勒发生冲突，而巴尔干不在条约覆盖范围内；1944年，斯大林没有直接向柏林推进，而是绕道巴尔干长途进军布达佩斯和维也纳，明确目的是划出一个巨大的苏联势力范围——同时也是挫败丘吉尔对该地区的图谋。但这并不意味着他当时打算把苏维埃制度引入这一地带，如他在1939年获得的波罗的海和波兰领土上所做的那样。相反，他是在审时度势地推行强权政治，这从他1944年对求和芬兰的宽大处理可以看出。曾建立卡累利阿—芬兰苏维埃社会主义共和国作为吸收整个芬兰的基地，但斯大林放弃了这一计划，换取几块有助于保护列宁格勒和摩尔曼斯克的领土，因为战争尚未打赢，他不想激怒盟国，而且当时他正在更重要的波兰问题上对他们施压。甚至战争打赢后，他仍相对谨慎地行事，以便在最重要的问题即德国问题上通过外交获得尽可能多的东西。
en: Having said this, it must be added that Soviet expansion was accelerated and hardened during 1946-1948 by Western efforts to contain it. The basic fact of the situation was Soviet conquest of most of the continent up to the Elbe and the Adriatic. This was in part the inevitable result of Hitler’s defeat, and in part the product of deliberate Soviet policy. Already in 1940 Stalin was coming into conflict with Hitler over the Balkans, which had not been covered by the Pact; and in 1944, rather than advancing directly on Berlin, Stalin took a long detour through the Balkans to Budapest and Vienna, with the clear aim of staking out an enormous Soviet sphere of influence—and also of thwarting Churchill’s designs on the area. But this does not mean that he aimed at that time to introduce the Soviet system into this zone, as he had done in the Baltic and Polish territories acquired in 1939. Rather, he was playing his power politics by ear, as is indicated by his leniency towards Finland when she sued for peace in 1944. A Karelo-Finnish Soviet Socialist Republic had been created as a base for absorbing the whole of Finland, but Stalin abandoned this project in return for slices of territory protecting Leningrad and Murmansk because he did not wish to rile the Allies while the war was not yet won, and while he was pressing them hard on the more important matter of Poland. Even after the war had been won, he still proceeded with relative caution in order to gain as much as possible through diplomacy in the most important matter of all, Germany.

zh: 当然，如同在波兰一样，罗马尼亚、匈牙利和保加利亚建立了人民阵线联合政府，内务和国防等关键部掌握在共产党人手中；社会党被施压与当地共产党合并，产生“统一工人党”。在捷克斯洛伐克，一个共产党占主导的人民阵线通过真正的选举上台；而在南斯拉夫，铁托领导下纯粹的共产党政权通过军事胜利掌权。因此到1946年末至1947年，人民阵线这个一贯不稳定的模式已在全东欧为共产党全面夺权搭好舞台，办法是对阵线中较温和的成员采用匈牙利马加什·拉科西所称的“萨拉米战术”。
en: Of course, as in Poland, Popular Front coalitions were installed in Romania, Hungary, and Bulgaria, with the key ministries of interior and defense in Communist hands; and socialist parties were pressured into merging with the local Communists to produce “United Workers’ Parties.” A Popular Front with Communist predominance came to power through genuine elections in Czechoslovakia, while a monochrome Communist regime under Tito gained power through military victory in Yugoslavia. Thus by late 1946-1947 the chronically unstable formula of the Popular Front had set the stage throughout Eastern Europe for full Communist takeovers through the application of what Matias Rakosi of Hungary called “salami tactics” to the more moderate members of the Fronts.

zh: 然而，直到斯大林确信不仅外交手段无法使他得到德国，而且西方“帝国主义者”正在采取行动破坏他辛苦赢得的东欧势力范围，屠刀才会落下。尽管德国三分之一处于苏联占领之下，这个桥头堡无法扩展为一个统治整个德国的“人民民主”政权。1945年7月的波茨坦会议规定德国将作为一个整体治理；然而西方盟国不会同意人民阵线，如他们在波兰问题上被迫同意的那样，因为这只会把苏联影响向西扩展到鲁尔和莱茵。苏联唯一可接受的替代方案是一个永久中立和非军事化的德国。但由于一旦苏军撤出，这一方案无法有效执行，到1947年他们退而把自己占领区当作一个单独单位治理，这一政策至少使他们永久留在易北河。盟国的回应是合并其三个占领区，组成不久后成为联邦共和国的实体。
en: Still, the cleaver would not fall until Stalin became convinced not only that diplomacy would not get him Germany but that the Western “imperialists” were acting to undermine his hard-won Eastern sphere of influence. Although a third of Germany was under Soviet occupation, this beachhead could not be expanded into a regime of People’s Democracy for the country as a whole. The Potsdam Conference of July 1945 had stipulated that Germany would be governed as a unit; the Western allies, however, would not agree to a Popular Front, as they had been forced to do in the case of Poland, because this would only extend Soviet influence westward to the Ruhr and the Rhine. The only alternative that was acceptable to the Soviets was a permanently neutral and demilitarized Germany. But since this option could not be effectively enforced if their troops were withdrawn, by 1947 they fell back on governing their zone as a separate unit, a policy that at least kept them permanently on the Elbe. The Allies answered by consolidating their three zones to form what would soon become the Federal Republic.

zh: 一旦战时合作以这种方式在德国问题上崩溃，西方就开始动员，保卫它此时认为受到威胁的阵地。第一步是1947年初的杜鲁门主义，据此美国接替英国在希腊和土耳其边境遏制苏联的角色。但西方的主要反击是马歇尔计划——1947年6月公布、1948年实施——美国据此着手恢复西欧经济，以结束可能使该地区易受共产主义影响的社会不稳定。马歇尔计划的援助最初也向苏联和东欧国家提供，这一提议部分是真诚的，部分是一种计谋。有一小段时间，斯大林似乎对接受援助犹豫不决；但在捷克人宣布接受后，莫斯科迅速断定美国援助将导致对其势力范围的资本主义颠覆——按作者的判断，情况确实会如此。于是苏联和此时已成为其“卫星国”的国家大声谴责马歇尔计划，整个欧洲被分成两个对立的社会经济地带。
en: Once wartime cooperation had collapsed in this manner over Germany, the West began to mobilize to defend what it now considered to be its menaced positions. The first step came in early 1947 with the Truman Doctrine, under which the United States took over the British role of containing the Soviets in Greece and along the Turkish frontier. But the main Western counterthrust was the Marshall Plan—unveiled in June 1947 and applied in 1948—whereby the United States undertook to rehabilitate the economies of Western Europe in order to end the social instability that could make the region vulnerable to Communism. Marshall Plan aid was at first offered to the countries of Eastern Europe, including the Soviet Union, an offer made in part sincerely and in part as a ruse. For a short time Stalin seemed hesitant about accepting the aid; but after the Czechs announced their acceptance, Moscow quickly concluded that American aid would result in the capitalist subversion of its zone—as indeed it would have. So the Soviet Union and what were now its “satellites” vociferously denounced the Marshall Plan, and Europe as a whole was divided into two antithetical socioeconomic zones.

zh: 于是大同盟瓦解了——先在波兰，然后在德国，然后遍及整个欧洲——因为苏联和西方社会组织模式本质上不相容。两者之间根本没有中间地带：一种模式要求多党制和市场经济，另一种要求一党制和命令经济。要把德国作为一个整体治理，要么盟国必须把自己的占领区苏维埃化，要么苏联必须不把自己的占领区苏维埃化。因此，这个问题的解决方式与十六世纪宗教战争中的做法相同：按军事分界线解决，依据的是——套用一句——

children: 谁的领地，谁的制度
cuius regio, eius societas

zh: ）。德国被分割，很快整个欧洲也被分割：苏联防线之后是社会主义，另一边则是苏联所称的“资本主义”、西方所称的“民主”。
en: Thus the Grand Alliance foundered—first in Poland, then in Germany, and then throughout Europe—because of the intrinsic incompatibility of the Soviet and Western modes of organizing society. There was simply no middle ground between the two: One mode required a multiparty system and a market, whereas the other required a single Party and a command economy. To govern Germany as a unit, either the Allies would have had to Sovietize their zones, or the Soviets would have had to refrain from Sovietizing theirs. Accordingly, the matter was decided the way sixteenth-century religious wars were: by military lines of demarcation on the basis of, to paraphrase,

children: cuius regio, eius societas

en: . Germany was partitioned, and soon the whole of Europe was divided as well: behind the Soviet lines there was socialism, and on the far side there was what the Soviets called “capitalism” and the West called “democracy.”

zh: 1945年后欧洲这种非同寻常的分割，常被解释为传统俄国帝国主义披着社会主义外衣的复兴。为支撑这一论点，人们有时把第三国际所在地莫斯科的革命弥赛亚主义，与旧莫斯科公国“莫斯科即第三罗马”（继罗马本身和君士坦丁堡之后）的宗教主张相提并论。此外，按照这种观点，俄国帝国主义被解释为国内俄国专制主义向外投射。于是斯大林1945年后的帝国事业，看起来就是他作为国内专制者、继承伊凡和彼得传统的逻辑对应物。
en: This extraordinary division of Europe after 1945 has often been explained as a resurgence of traditional Russian imperialism in socialist guise. To clinch this argument, the parallel is at times drawn between the revolutionary messianism of Moscow, seat of the Third International, and the religious claims of “Moscow the Third Rome” (after Rome itself and Constantinople) of old Muscovy. In this view, moreover, Russian imperialism is explained as the projection outward of Russian despotism at home. Thus Stalin’s imperial career after 1945 appears as the logical counterpart of his role as domestic autocrat in the lineage of Ivan and Peter.

zh: 然而，旧俄国与苏联之间的线性连续性，在国际事务上并不比在国内事务上更成立。诚然，旧俄国曾大力扩张，但它是按欧洲列强的传统方式扩张。莫斯科大公国在四个世纪里成长为从波罗的海延伸到太平洋的庞大帝国——但小小的英国在同一时期扩张到统治世界四分之一陆地面积，法国也尽力在全球竞争。英国把帝国理想化为“白人的负担”，或法国自诩帝国传播自由、平等、博爱，其中的弥赛亚主义，与俄国向君士坦丁堡和海峡的泛斯拉夫推进中的弥赛亚主义一样多。
en: Yet linear continuity between old Russia and the Soviet Union works no better for international than for internal affairs. To be sure, old Russia expanded mightily, but she did so in the traditional manner of a European great power. Thus, the Grand Duchy of Moscow grew over four centuries to become a huge empire stretching from the Baltic to the Pacific—but little Britain expanded during the same period to rule a quarter of the world’s land surface, while France did her best to compete around the globe. And there was as much messianism in Britain’s idealization of empire as the “white man’s burden,” or in France’s conceit that empire spread liberty, equality, and fraternity, as there was in Russia’s pan-Slav drive to Constantinople and the Straits.

zh: 然而事实上，在所有这些扩张案例中，意识形态都次于地缘政治利益。因此俄国像所有其他欧洲列强一样，扩张范围以其军事实力和经济实力所能达到的程度为限。这意味着，与更有活力的西方国家不同，她无法把力量投射到海外，只能吸收欧亚大陆边缘从波兰到高加索、突厥斯坦到满洲的毗连地区。此外，旧俄国在任何地方都没有寻求强加一种新制度，而只是其专制—军事控制。
en: In fact, however, in all of these cases of expansion ideology was secondary to geopolitical interest. Thus Russia, like all other European powers, went only as far as her military force and her economic power could take her. And this meant that, unlike the more dynamic Western states, she could not project her power overseas but was able only to absorb contiguous areas around the rim of Eurasia from Poland to the Caucasus to Turkistan to Manchuria. Moreover, nowhere did old Russia seek to impose a new system other than her autocratic-military control.

children: 〔译注〕俄国帝国曾在北美经营阿拉斯加等海外领地，1867年将其售予美国；因此“无法把力量投射到海外”的概括并非没有例外。
〔译注〕俄国帝国曾在北美经营阿拉斯加等海外领地，1867年将其售予美国；因此“无法把力量投射到海外”的概括并非没有例外。

zh: 然而苏联不仅拥有俄国权力的传统手段；她还拥有社会主义思想这一武器。因此在斯大林治下，苏联人把他们的制度强加到其武力所及之处。而在这一范围之外，苏联把社会主义思想与反法西斯情绪结合起来，从而通过人民阵线和“争取和平的斗争”把苏联权力投射到全世界。稍微前瞻一下：在斯大林继承者治下，苏联人的意识形态立场产生了“民族解放战争”的代理力量，用以对抗欧洲殖民主义和美国帝国主义。于是苏联可以操纵西方国家的工会；她可以在东亚、中东、非洲和拉丁美洲找到受其庇护的势力；她可以动员全世界的知识分子。但很难想象沙皇俄国在古巴或安哥拉建立桥头堡，或在西方知识分子中招募其社会制度的仰慕者。斯大林曾轻蔑地问：“教皇有多少个师？”他对精神力量的玩世不恭是虚伪的，因为他本人就统率着意识形态战士的军团。正是这种意识形态化的政治战斗序列，产生了1945年后欧洲前所未有的分裂以及由此而来的冷战。于是铁幕两边存在的人民阵线在1947—1948年解体。在法国和意大利，基督教民主党人、社会党人和共产党人的联合政府从抵抗运动中产生；两国共产党都是最大群体，拥有超过三分之一的选民。莫斯科在这些国家确实拥有比东欧大部分地区更大的可操作基础。然而通过夺权来利用这一资源会太危险，部分因为苏联在国内太弱，无法提供任何直接援助，部分因为美国可能的反应。因此随着大同盟崩溃，两国共产党没有超出声势浩大的“反帝国主义”鼓动。但这已足够吓人，使他们的伙伴于1947年初在两国政府中把他们排挤出去。共产党人随后发动一波准起义性罢工，抗议马歇尔计划和美国的“战争叫嚣”与“法西斯主义”。其目的无疑是制造一种“牵制”：在苏联巩固其在东方成果的同时，让西方政府在国内不得安宁。
en: The Soviet Union, however, had not only the traditional means of Russian power at her disposal; she also had the weapon of the socialist idea. Thus, under Stalin the Soviets imposed their system wherever their arms reached. And beyond this reach, the Soviet Union adjoined to the socialist idea the antifascist reflex, thereby projecting Soviet power worldwide through Popular Fronts and the “struggle for peace.” To anticipate a bit, under Stalin’s successors the Soviets’ ideological stance yielded the proxy power of “wars of national liberation” against European colonialism and American imperialism. Thus the Soviet Union could manipulate the labor unions of Western countries; she could find clients in East Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Latin America; and she could mobilize intellectuals the world over. But it is difficult to see tsarist Russia establishing beachheads in Cuba or Angola, or recruiting admirers of her social system among the intelligentsia of the West. Stalin one derisively asked, “How many divisions has the pope?” His cynicism regarding spiritual power was disingenuous, for he himself commanded legions of ideological warriors. It is this ideologized battle order of politics that yielded the unprecedented division of Europe after 1945 and the resulting Cold War. Thus the Popular Fronts that had existed on both sides of the iron curtain dissolved in 1947-1948. In France and Italy, coalition governments of Christian Democrats, Socialists, and Communists had emerged from the resistance; and in both countries the Communists constituted the largest group, with over a third of the electorate. Moscow indeed had a larger base to work with in these countries than in most of Eastern Europe. Yet it would have been too dangerous to exploit this resource by taking power, in part because the Soviets were too weak at home to offer any direct assistance, and in part because of the probable American reaction. So as the Grand Alliance crumbled, the Communist parties in both countries did not go beyond strident “anti-imperialist” agitation. But this was frightening enough to cause their partners to force them out of the government in both countries in early 1947. The Communists then launched a wave of quasi-insurrectionary strikes to protest against the Marshall Plan and American “war-mongering” and “fascism.” The purpose of this was no doubt to create a “diversion”: Western governments were kept off balance at home while the Soviet Union consolidated its gains in the East.

zh: 简言之，斯大林在继续其1930年代政策，即利用一场非常真实的国外革命运动来推进苏维埃国家的利益。而这又意味着，一边煽起革命之火，一边确保它不致公开燎原。这一手法得到一场新“和平运动”的补充，后者此时以原子武器为中心，反对美国和西欧重整军备。只要冷战和苏联持续，“反法西斯主义”和“争取和平的斗争”，加上人民阵线挥之不去的道德光环，就将是苏联武库中较有力的武器。
en: In short, Stalin was continuing his 1930s policy of utilizing a very real foreign revolutionary movement to further the interests of the Soviet state. And this meant, once again, stoking those revolutionary fires while at the same time insuring that they would not lead to an open conflagration. This technique was supplemented by a new “peace movement” that was now centered on atomic weapons and directed against American and Western European rearmament. For as long as the Cold War and the Soviet Union would endure, “anti-fascism” and “the struggle for peace,” combined with a lingering moral aura of the Popular Front, would be among the more potent weapons in the Soviet arsenal.

zh: 在同一时期，人民民主国家的人民阵线模式瓦解，左派取得优势。这些政权1945年在共产党领导下建立，直到1947年才巩固对国家事务的控制。一个主要原因是，除南斯拉夫和捷克斯洛伐克外，东欧国家的共产党人不足以组成政府：1945年波兰只有一万名党员，罗马尼亚只有一千名。（从这么微小的罗马尼亚核心竟能造出齐奥塞斯库那样包罗一切的暴政，实属非同寻常——不过，在俄国本身，1917年十月夺权时也只有十二万布尔什维克。）因此与其他政党联合是管理事务的实际必需，同时党在苏联顾问帮助下物色并培训自己的干部。谨慎也是可取的，因为几乎到处民族情绪都是反苏的，新政府被视为占领政权。
en: During these same years the formula of the Popular Front broke down in the People’s Democracies in favor of the Left. Installed in 1945 under Communist leadership, these regimes did not consolidate their control over national affairs until 1947. A major reason for this was that, with the exception of Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia, East European countries did not have enough Communists to form a government: in 1945 there were only 10,000 Party members in Poland, and 1,000 in Romania. (It is extraordinary that such an all-encompassing tyranny as that of Ceausescu could be created out of this miniscule Romanian nucleus—but then, in Russia itself, there were only 120,000 Bolsheviks when they took over in October 1917.) A coalition with other parties was therefore a practical necessity for managing affairs while the Party, with the help of Soviet advisors, acquired and trained its own cadres. Caution was also advisable because almost everywhere the national sentiment was anti-Soviet, and the new governments were viewed as occupation regimes.

zh: 但当1947年马歇尔计划的“威胁”出现，不仅诱惑捷克斯洛伐克，也诱惑波兰时，共产党的霸权立即被绝对化。在波兰，操纵选举之后，社会党人最终与共产党人合并为单一政党。然而最戏剧性的案例是捷克斯洛伐克。1948年2月，十二名非共产党部长辞职，抗议共产党同僚对行政的蚕食式接管；他们希望引发选举，而他们完全可以合理地指望获胜。共产党人在左翼社会民主党人帮助下随即结束人民阵线，完全掌权。应当指出，这场政变完全是一场捷克斯洛伐克行动，因为当时该国没有苏联军队。而且，尽管仅仅由于苏联邻近而对捷克人施加了间接压力，但如果一个非共产党政府成立，斯大林要干预仍会是一件大事。捷克斯洛伐克是在人民阵线的危险演变中走上了共产主义道路。
en: But when the “threat” of the Marshall Plan appeared in 1947, tempting not only Czechoslovakia but also Poland, Communist hegemony was immediately made absolute. In Poland, after rigged elections, the Socialists were finally merged with the Communists into a single party. The most dramatic case, however, was that of Czechoslovakia. In February 1948 twelve non-Communist ministers resigned in protest against their Communist colleagues’ creeping takeover of the administration; their hope was to provoke elections that they could quite reasonably expect to win. The Communists, aided by the left Social Democrats, thereupon ended the Popular Front and took over completely. It should be pointed out that this coup was entirely a Czechoslovak operation, for there were no Soviet troops in the country at the time. And, even though indirect pressure was exerted on the Czechoslovaks by the mere proximity of the Soviet Union, it would nonetheless have been a major matter for Stalin to intervene if a non-Communist government had been formed. Czechoslovakia became Communist through the perilous dynamic of the Popular Front.

zh: 任何人民阵线本质上都是不稳定、过渡性的联盟。之所以如此，是因为人民阵线由两种不相容的政治要素组成——一边是宪政民主的拥护者，另一边是列宁主义独裁的追求者。把两者维系在一起的，至少暂时地，是这样一种信念：双方都站在“左派”一边，即都反对企图以威权政权取代宪政政府的“右派”。但这是权宜婚姻，不是真正的结合。此外，人民阵线还存在其他含混之处。其自由派或基督教民主党成员不想要社会主义，只要福利改良主义；而其社会党和共产党成员虽然都说想要社会主义，实际所指大不相同：前者只向往一个全面的福利国家，后者则渴望苏联模式的全面社会主义。
en: Any Popular Front is an inherently unstable and transitional alignment. This is so because a Popular Front is composed of two incompatible political elements—adherents of constitutional democracy on the one hand, and aspirants to Leninist dictatorship on the other. The two are held together, at least temporarily, by the conviction that they are both on the “Left” in the sense of being opposed to a “Right” that seeks to replace constitutional government with an authoritarian regime. But this is a marriage of convenience, not a genuine union. A Popular Front is beset, moreover, by other ambiguities. Its liberal or Christian Democratic members do not want socialism, only welfare reformism; and its Socialist and Communist members, though they both say they want socialism, in fact mean very different things by it: The former aspires only to a comprehensive welfare state, while the latter desires integral socialism on the Soviet model.

zh: 因此，这种阵线中的共产党成分和非共产党成分，都不能诚实地对待自己的“伙伴”。每一方都必须试图利用另一方达到自己的目的。自由派和社会党人寻求共产党支持以渡过难关、实现某些社会改革，如1936年的法国；共产党人利用暂时盟友夺取全部权力，如1948年的捷克斯洛伐克。然而双方并不真正对称。自由派，尤其是社会党人和某些基督教民主党人，始终容易受到左派团结神话的诱惑。共产党人没有这种幻想，因为他们自列宁以来就知道自己是唯一真正的左派；因此他们能比温和的同僚更无情、更玩世不恭——如他们在1945年后每个人民民主国家所做的那样。这些含混之处同样适用于国际事务，如三巨头关于波兰的谈判，或1946—1948年冷战酝酿期间西方关于苏联意图的辩论。
en: Hence, neither the Communist nor the non-Communist component of such a Front can deal honestly with its “partner.” Each must try to use the other for its own ends. The liberals and the Socialists seek Communist support to get through a difficult pass and to achieve certain social reforms, as in France in 1936; the Communists use their temporary allies to climb to full power, as in Czechoslovakia in 1948. Yet the two sides are not really symmetrical. The liberals, especially the Socialists and certain Christian Democrats, are perpetually vulnerable to the mystique of the unity of the Left. The Communists have no such illusions, for they have known since Lenin that they are the one true Left; they can therefore behave more ruthlessly and cynically than their softer colleagues—as they did in each of the People’s Democracies after 1945. And these ambiguities apply equally to international affairs, as in the negotiations among the Big Three over Poland, or in the Western debates about Soviet intentions during the buildup to the Cold War in 1946-1948.

zh: 因此，鉴于任何人民阵线都有内部矛盾，这种联盟只能相当快地结束，并以两种方式之一告终。要么非共产党人因共产党人的力量而警觉，把他们赶出政府，如1947年的法国和意大利；要么共产党人利用这种力量赶走昔日盟友，如次年的布拉格政变。但人民阵线绝不可能以建立一个持久的“民主社会主义”告终，即计划经济与人道宪政主义的混合，它曾以不同名称被称为“第三条道路”“趋同”或“人道面孔的社会主义”。然而，这种结果可能实现的幻觉将和共产主义本身一样长久，尽管有种种相反的实际证据。
en: Given the internal contradictions of any Popular Front, therefore, this kind of alliance can only end fairly quickly and in one of two fashions. Either the non-Communists become alarmed at the Communists’ strength and force them out of the government, as in France and Italy in 1947; or the Communists use that strength to force out their erstwhile allies, as in the Prague Coup of the following year. But a Popular Front can never end with the establishment of an enduring “democratic socialism,” that mixture of a planned economy with a humane constitutionalism that has variously been known as “the third way,” “convergence,” or “socialism with a human face.” Yet the illusion that this outcome was possible would endure for as long as Communism itself, despite all empirical evidence to the contrary.

zh: 而在1948年人民阵线失败之后，这种证据继续增长。下一个人民阵线1970至1973年在智利尝试；当基督教民主党人不愿约束他们昔日的盟友萨尔瓦多·阿连德——他正走向卡斯特罗式社会主义——时，他们被右翼的皮诺切特将军碾过，实验告终。另一个人民阵线1975年出现在葡萄牙；在一场军事革命委员会和共产党领导下的大幅左转之后，实验被社会党人和自由派结束。人民阵线综合征的最后一次出现是在1970年代后期，表现为欧洲共产主义向社会党和基督教民主党示好。这些倡议最终形成弗朗索瓦·密特朗1981—1984年非常温和的人民阵线联盟；当社会党人放弃其“从资本主义向社会主义过渡”的承诺，随后把令自己难堪的同僚赶出内阁时，它结束了。
en: And that evidence continued to grow after the Popular Front’s failure of 1948. The next Popular Front was tried in Chile between 1970 and 1973; it ended when the Christian Democrats, unwilling to rein in their one-time ally Salvador Allende as he moved towards a Castro-like socialism, were overrun on their right by General Pinochet. Another Popular Front appeared in Portugal in 1975; after a great leftward lunge under the leadership of a military revolutionary council and the Communist Party, the experiment was ended by the Socialists and the liberals. The final appearance of the Popular Front syndrome occurred in the late 1970s, in the form of Eurocommunist overtures to Socialists and Christian Democrats. These initiatives culminated in the very modest Popular Front coalition of François Mitterrand in 1981-1984; it ended when the Socialists backed off from their commitment to the “transition from capitalism to socialism” and then dropped their compromising colleagues from the cabinet.

en: Thus the Popular Front formula that had been created in France a half-century earlier ended in that same country and so faded from political history for lack of a credibly progressive Communism. But the mystique of the united Left that reached its high point of practical effectiveness in Eastern and Western Europe in the years 1945-1948 surely has not disappeared along with Communism. It is too organic a part of modern politics not to reappear eventually, albeit in new political guises.

zh: 冷战的顶点，以及随之而来的地球两极化为“社会主义阵营”和“自由世界”，发生在1948—1950年。1948年，当共产党人在布拉格接管时，西方盟国正在建立统一的西德，并推出新的强势德国马克。苏联人把此理解为最终德国重新武装的前奏；夏天，他们以封锁柏林回应，目的与其说是夺取该城，不如说是破坏盟国的整个德国行动。这一努力失败了，1949年德意志联邦共和国正式成立。作为回应，同年苏联人把他们占领区提升为“德国土地上第一个工农国家”，名为德意志民主共和国。也在1949年，北大西洋公约组织（NATO）成立，尽管最初不包括西德。
en: The culmination of the Cold War, and with it the polarization of the planet into a “socialist camp” and a “free world,” occurred in 1948-1950. In 1948, as the Communists were taking over in Prague, the Western allies were creating a unified West Germany with a new, strong Deutsche mark. This the Soviets construed as a prelude to eventual German rearmament; in the summer they answered with a blockade of Berlin that was designed not so much to take the city as to disrupt the whole German operation of the Allies. This effort failed, and in 1949 the German Federal Republic was formally established. In response, that same year the Soviets promoted their zone of occupation to the status of “the first workers’ and peasants’ state on German soil” under the name German Democratic Republic. And also in 1949, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) was formed, though it did not initially include West Germany.

zh: 同一时期，苏联人完成了对东欧“集团”的巩固。1947年，他们已建立共产国际的继承者，名为共产党情报局（Cominform）。自1945年以来，欧洲共产主义运动大大壮大；法国和意大利第一次出现群众性政党，东方有六个政党执政。情报局的目的是协调这些政党反对帝国主义和世界主义的斗争——或者用该组织机关报的话说，“为持久和平，为人民民主”。
en: In the same period, the Soviets completed their consolidation of the Eastern “bloc.” Already in 1947 they had created a successor to the Comintern under the name Communist Information Bureau, or Cominform. Since 1945 the Communist movement in Europe had grown enormously; mass Parties now existed for the first time in France and Italy, and six Parties were in power in the East. The purpose of the Cominform was to coordinate the struggle of these Parties against imperialism and cosmopolitanism—or, as the organization’s newssheet put it, “for a lasting peace, for a people’s democracy.”

zh: 然而，这种集中指导的努力很快与唯一真正独立的新共产主义政权即南斯拉夫发生冲突。

该政权有魅力的领导人铁托虽然忠于斯大林和苏联社会主义模式，却是依靠自己的力量完成了革命；在胜利的狂喜中，他此时想与阿尔巴尼亚和保加利亚建立一个巴尔干联邦。斯大林否决了这一雄心勃勃的倡议，因为他不想在新的共产主义帝国中出现竞争性权力中心。在两位领导人激烈的书信往来之后，1948年夏天情报局公开谴责铁托，希望激起南斯拉夫共产党人把他赶下台。然而，一场长期诋毁运动未能达到目的，因为南斯拉夫党可以说是自立的组织，其机构听命于本国的领导中心。
en: This effort at centralized direction, however, soon provoked a conflict with the only genuinely independent new Communist regime, that of Yugoslavia.

The regime’s charismatic leader, Tito, though devoted to Stalin and the Soviet model of socialism, had made his revolution on his own, and in the euphoria of victory he now wished to create a Balkan federation with Albania and Bulgaria. Stalin vetoed this ambitious initiative because he wanted no rival centers of power in the new Communist empire. After an acrimonious correspondence between the two leaders, in the summer of 1948 the Cominform publicly condemned Tito in the hope of arousing the Yugoslav Communists to oust him. A prolonged campaign of vilification failed to achieve this, however, because the Yugoslav Party was, so to speak, an autocephalous organization with its own apparat taking orders from its own center.

zh: 因此，在苏联以外第一批共产主义政权上台仅三年后，就变得明显：它们的列宁主义集中化结构提供了创造与原列宁主义体系竞争的权力极的可能性。这表明，世界社会主义体系只有直接由莫斯科控制才能保持统一。尽管这一局面令斯大林不安，苏联在世界共产主义运动中的威望仍然压倒一切。结果，南斯拉夫的背离没有遭到军事干预回应，铁托被当作一个遭到排斥的异端，最终会在偏居一隅的孤立中自行衰亡。
en: Thus, only three years after the first Communist regimes outside the Soviet Union had come to power, it became apparent that their centralized Leninist structures offered the possibility of creating rival poles of power to the original Leninist system. This demonstrated that the world socialist system would remain unified only if it were directly controlled from Moscow. Although this situation was disturbing to Stalin, Soviet prestige in the world Communist movement nonetheless remained overwhelming. As a consequence, the Yugoslav defection was not answered with military intervention, and Tito was treated as an outcast heretic who would eventually wither away in provincial isolation.

zh: 集体化此前一直缓慢进行以免激起农民抵抗，此时在东欧被仓促推向完成；这场运动最终除波兰外到处成功。此外，雄心勃勃的五年计划启动，不可避免地强调冶金——如诺瓦胡塔，波兰的马格尼托哥尔斯克。教会也受到迫害，其领导人常受公审，如匈牙利的明曾蒂红衣主教。此外，与西方的一切接触被切断，文化按安德烈·日丹诺夫的准则加以规划。东方的“兄弟”党正朝着成为老大哥的缩小版的方向发展。到1950年，苏维埃帝国确实成了一个“集团”。
en: Collectivization, which until then had been proceeding only slowly so as not to arouse peasant resistance, was now precipitously pushed to completion in Eastern Europe; this campaign eventually succeeded everywhere except in Poland. In addition, ambitious Five-Year Plans were launched, with the inevitable emphasis on metallurgy—as at Nowa Huta, the Polish equivalent of Magnitogorsk. The churches were also persecuted, and their leaders often given show trials, as was the case with Cardinal Mindszenty in Hungary. Moreover, all contacts with the West were severed, and culture was planned according to the canons of Andrei Zhdanov. The “fraternal” Parties of the East were well on their way to becoming lesser replicas of Big Brother. By 1950 the Soviet empire had indeed become a “bloc.”

zh: 与此同时，当中国共产党1949年10月终于掌权时，仍自称“国际工人运动”的共产主义在东方取得了更大的进展。然而这不是莫斯科的作为，而是毛泽东及其同志送来的意外且并不完全受欢迎的礼物。
en: At the same time, “the international workers’ movement,” as Communism still called itself, gathered in even greater gains in the East when the Chinese Party at last came to power in October of 1949. This, however, was not of Moscow’s doing but an unexpected and not entirely welcome gift of Mao Zedong and his comrades.

zh: 战争结束时，斯大林显然没有预料到中国共产党胜利。在苏联人摧毁满洲的日本军队后，他首先关心的是通过接管通往符拉迪沃斯托克的中东铁路以及大连和旅顺两个不冻港，确保自己在该地区的利益。为确保这些权益，1945年8月斯大林与蒋介石签订《友好同盟条约》，其中承诺不干预中国内战。他没有遵守这一承诺。斯大林从满洲的苏联基地向中国共产党人提供缴获的日本装备；次年，在苏联占领结束时接管满洲的是共产党人，而不是国民党人。然而这并不意味着斯大林预期毛泽东征服全中国。相反，他似乎相信美国绝不会容忍这样的结果，因此毛泽东最终会控制华北一个依赖苏联支持和保护的共产主义区域。斯大林对中国的期望，大概类似于他在朝鲜实际取得的成果；在那里，他占领了分配给自己的半岛一半，建立了一个最初几乎不比东欧同类政权更独立的共产主义政权。
en: At the end of the war Stalin had clearly not expected a Chinese Communist victory. After the Soviets had destroyed the Japanese army in Manchuria, his first concern had been to secure his interests in that area by taking over the Chinese Eastern Railroad leading to Vladivostok and the warm-water ports of Dairen and Port Arthur. To secure his title to all of this, in August 1945 Stalin signed a Treaty of Friendship and Alliance with Chiang Kai-shek, in which he promised not to intervene in the Chinese civil war. This promise he did not keep. From the Soviet base in Manchuria Stalin supplied the Chinese Communists with captured Japanese equipment; and the next year it was the Communists, not the Nationalists, who took over Manchuria at the end of the Soviet occupation. This does not mean, however, that Stalin expected Mao to conquer all of China. Rather, he seems to have believed that America would never tolerate such an outcome, and that Mao, therefore, would wind up controlling a Communist zone in north China that would be dependent on Soviet support and protection. Stalin’s expectations for China were probably similar to what he had actually achieved in Korea; there he had occupied his allotted half of the peninsula and had established a Communist regime that was at first hardly more independent than its analogues in Eastern Europe.

zh: 然而到1949年，中国共产党出人意料地把其“区域”扩展到整个中国大陆，这造成了一个东欧根本无法提供先例的局面。两个共产主义巨人之间的关系将不可避免地是一种并不平等的伙伴关系。而且双方情绪都很复杂。尽管毛泽东真心钦佩苏联和斯大林个人成就，并把两者当作榜样，但他仍对苏联在中国共产党人数十年斗争期间、尤其是最后关键几年支持如此吝啬感到不满。斯大林真心满意中国革命给共产主义力量与威望——以及他作为最高共产主义领袖的个人地位——带来的巨大提升，但他也对出现一个莫斯科不能直接控制的革命权威中心感到担忧。然而两位党领袖也意识到，世界共产主义统一的神话，乃至现实，对各自的力量和整个运动的进展都不可或缺。
en: By 1949, however, the Chinese Party had unexpectedly expanded its “zone” to cover the whole of continental China, and this created a situation for which Eastern Europe could in no way offer a precedent. The relationship between the two Communist giants would have to be one of partnership without being one of equality. Sentiments on both sides, moreover, were mixed. Although Mao genuinely admired both the Soviet Union and the personal accomplishments of Stalin, and took both as his model, he was nonetheless resentful of the fact that Soviet support during the Chinese Communists’ decades of struggle had been so niggardly, especially in the last crucial years. And Stalin was genuinely satisfied with the enormous boost to Communist power and prestige—as well as to his personal position as supreme Communist leader—that the Chinese Revolution had provided, but he was nonetheless concerned by the emergence of a center of revolutionary authority that Moscow did not control directly. Yet both Party leaders were also aware that the myth, indeed the reality, of world Communist unity was indispensable to the strength of each, and to the progress of the movement as a whole.

zh: 因此，斯大林与毛泽东打交道时，比与铁托打交道时谨慎得多。1949年底毛泽东刚掌权就来到莫斯科，参加庆祝斯大林七十岁生日，斯大林同意放弃1945年在东北取得的权益，并向中国提供经济和军事援助。尽管援助绝不算慷慨，它意味着中国将遵循苏联发展模式，而中国人本来也真心相信这一模式。毛泽东则刻意恭敬对待斯大林较高的地位，但也坚持中国的尊严。简言之，甚至在新苏中关系开始时，就有紧张的先兆，如果情况变化，紧张可能恶化。斯大林在世时关系保持相对平稳，因为双方都无法想象共产主义会分裂却仍繁荣，这意味着所有共产党人都必须服从斯大林。铁托对毛泽东来说，正如对斯大林一样，是个异端。
en: Accordingly, Stalin was much more careful in his dealings with Mao than he had been in those with Tito. When Mao came to Moscow at the end of 1949—right after taking power—to help celebrate Stalin’s seventieth birthday, Stalin agreed to give up his 1945 gains in Manchuria and to provide China with economic and military assistance. Although the aid was by no means generous, it meant that China would follow the Soviet model of development, which the Chinese genuinely believed in anyway. Mao, for his part, was studiously deferential to Stalin’s superior status but also insistent on Chinese dignity. In short, even at the start of the new Soviet-Chinese relationship, there were intimations of tension that could worsen if circumstances changed. Relations remained relatively smooth while Stalin lived because it was inconceivable to both sides that Communism could fragment and yet prosper, and this meant that all Communists would have to defer to Stalin. Tito was as much a heretic to Mao as he was to Stalin.

zh: 回顾起来很清楚，中国革命是共产主义成功的顶点：从易北河到中国海，各政权之间确实存在政治和道义上的统一，尽管未必有组织上的统一；共产主义向前发展的势头似乎不可阻挡。这此时成了西方的严重担忧。而共产主义在全欧亚的胜利，看来确实成了斯大林的目标，因为中国革命的另一个产物是他决定巩固并扩大他此前在朝鲜取得的成果。这一过度自信的决定产生了共产主义与西方力量之间的第一次武装冲突。
en: In retrospect it is clear that the Chinese Revolution was the apogee of Communist success: A political and a moral, if not an organizational, unity among regimes did in fact exist, extending from the Elbe to the China Seas, and the forward momentum of Communist gain seemed to be unstoppable. This was now an acute worry to the West. And the victory of Communism throughout Eurasia does seem to have become Stalin’s objective, for another product of the Chinese Revolution was his decision to round off his previous gains in Korea. This overconfident decision produced the first armed conflict between Communist and Western forces.

zh: 斯大林七十寿辰庆典的客人之一，是北朝鲜的金日成。此时苏美占领军都已撤出半岛。金日成于是向斯大林建议，从北方军事推进将在南方引发革命，从而产生一个完全共产主义的朝鲜，这一剧本可以呈现为一场内战。斯大林接受了这一提议，同意向北朝鲜提供现代化军备。他似乎盘算，如果美国人前一年把整个中国拱手交给了共产党人，他们就不会为南朝鲜这样无足轻重的地方干预。看来也咨询了毛泽东，鉴于他对“纸老虎”的蔑视，他没有反对。
en: One of the guests at Stalin’s seventieth anniversary was Kim Il Sung of North Korea. By this time both Soviet and American occupation troops had been withdrawn from the peninsula. Kim therefore suggested to Stalin that a military advance from the north would produce a revolution in the south and thus a wholly Communist Korea, a scenario that could be presented as a civil war. Stalin accepted this proposal and agreed to supply North Korea with up-to-date armaments. He seems to have calculated that if the Americans had abandoned the whole of China to Communism the previous year, they would not intervene for something so insignificant as South Korea. It seems that Mao Zedong was also consulted, and given his scorn for “the Paper Tiger,” he did not object.

zh: 大问题又是：斯大林打算让这场冒险走多远？我们最好的猜测是，这一次他希望走得相当远。他刚在欧洲柏林封锁问题上受挫。与此同时，中国的事态为整个东亚的革命收获开辟了前景。因此，他理应在太平洋战区寻求新的机会。的确，斯大林和毛泽东都在1948年承认了胡志明的临时政府；同时，马来亚有共产党叛乱，印度尼西亚有共产党政变企图。可以想象，在这种情况下，通常谨慎的斯大林会突然接受毛泽东激进得多的想法，选择在亚洲全面推进共产主义。特别是，日本反对美国占领当局的共产党活动出现高涨；而在斯大林心中，共产主义朝鲜的蓝图可能是东京出现中立主义、甚至红色政权的前奏，这一结果既会让美国人不舒服，也会包抄中国人。这些前景尽管看似荒诞，我们应当记住，斯大林此时也许已经精神失常；因为他显然在国内也在盘算同样荒诞的事情。因此朝鲜冒险很可能表明，斯大林此时力图在全欧亚获取最大限度的帝国利益。正如法国谚语所说，胃口是吃出来的。很明显，在斯大林最后几年，他的国际野心增长了，而对“帝国主义者”的恐惧减弱了。
en: The great question is, once again, how far did Stalin intend to go with this adventure? Our best conjecture is that this time he hoped to go quite far. He had just been frustrated in Europe over the Berlin blockade. At the same time, however, events in China opened the prospect of revolutionary gains throughout East Asia. Therefore, it would be logical for him to seek new fortunes in the Pacific theater. And indeed both Stalin and Mao recognized Ho Chi Minh’s provisional government in 1948; at the same time, there was a Communist insurgency in Malaya and an attempted Communist coup in Indonesia. It is conceivable that under these circumstances the usually cautious Stalin would have suddenly become receptive to the much more militant ideas of Mao, and to have opted for a general Communist advance in Asia. In particular, there was a surge of Communist activism in Japan against the American occupation government; and the design for a Communist Korea could have been, in Stalin’s mind, a prelude to a neutralist, or even a Red, regime in Tokyo, an eventuality that would both discomfort the Americans and outflank the Chinese. As fantastic as these perspectives might seem, we should remember that Stalin was now, perhaps, deranged; for he was clearly contemplating equally fantastic things at home. So the Korean adventure is quite probably a sign that Stalin was now out for maximum imperial advantage throughout Eurasia. As the French saying goes, appetite comes with eating. It is clear that in Stalin’s last years his international ambition had grown while his fear of the “imperialists” had diminished.

zh: 但无论朝鲜冒险背后的完整故事是什么，开战决定结果是一个重大误算。西方对共产主义侵略意图的所有残余怀疑都消失了；尽管朝鲜战争被更多归咎于毛泽东而不是斯大林，共产主义到处被视为迫在眉睫的威胁。美国根据联合国授权介入朝鲜战争；尽管战争以僵持结束，此时已清楚美国不会在对共产主义的军事行动上退缩。在西方，德国重新武装变得不可避免，北约开始获得真正的军事能力。美国着手系统建设常规和核军备，苏联也照做。因此朝鲜战争标志着第一阶段冷战——斯大林元帅主导的冷战——达到高潮及最危险的时刻。而在这场战争中间，他退出了历史。
en: But whatever the full story behind the Korean adventure may be, the decision for war turned out to be a major miscalculation. All remaining doubts in the West about Communism’s aggressive intentions vanished, and although the Korean War was blamed more on Mao than on Stalin, Communism everywhere was now viewed as an imminently threatening force. The United States intervened in Korea under a mandate from the United Nations, and although the war ended in a stalemate, it was now clear that America would not hold back from military action against Communism. In the West, German rearmament became inevitable, and NATO began to acquire a genuine military capability. The United States undertook a systematic buildup of both conventional and nuclear armaments, and the Soviet Union did the same. The Korean War thus marks the culmination and the most dangerous moment of the first Cold War, that of Marshal Stalin. And in its midst he made his exit from history.

en: EXIT THE RED KHAN

zh: 斯大林最后的四年给这个政权带来了又一场危机。他在过去二十年里发展起来的制度与做法，此时开始损害制度本身的运转。而在这最后一次自上而下的革命尝试中，可以说他的偏执已经发展到精神错乱。
en: Stalin’s last four years brought yet another crisis to the regime. The institutions and practices he had developed over the previous two decades now began to work against the functioning of the system itself. And in this final attempt at revolution from above, a case can be made that his paranoia had become dementia.

zh: 战后年代，斯大林靠让一帮近侍与另一帮近侍相互制衡来统治。莫洛托夫、卡冈诺维奇等20世纪20年代进入政治局的元老，影响力开始不及1939年以后升到这一级别的人。在后者当中，战争结束时格奥尔基·马林科夫正得势。然而在1946—1947年，他被日丹诺夫及其来自列宁格勒的近侍们盖过，其中包括才华出众的经济学家尼古拉·沃兹涅先斯基——他也是政治局委员，曾在战争期间主持苏联经济。1948年日丹诺夫早逝（很可能是自然死亡）后，马林科夫与贝利亚结盟重新居于权力中心；1949—1950年，两人在“列宁格勒案”中策划了对沃兹涅先斯基及其他日丹诺夫盟友的清洗和处决。由于这是十年来首次清洗政治局委员，它标志着新危机的开端。同样在1949年，莫洛托夫、伏罗希洛夫和米高扬被免去部长职务；莫洛托夫的妻子被捕流放；斯大林还开始说，莫洛托夫和伏罗希洛夫自1918年起就是英国间谍。与此同时，另一位较年轻的竞争者赫鲁晓夫被从基辅调到莫斯科，以制衡马林科夫。
en: In the postwar years Stalin governed by balancing one clique of retainers against another. Such elders as Molotov and Kaganovich, who had entered the Politburo in the 1920s, began to lose influence to men who attained that rank after 1939. Among the latter, at the end of the war Georgii Malenkov was ascendant. In 1946-1947, however, he was eclipsed by Zhdanov and his retainers from Leningrad, including the talented economist Nikolai Voznesenskii, also a Politburo member, who had managed the Soviet economy during the war. Upon Zhdanov’s early but probably natural death in 1948, Malenkov returned to the front rank in alliance with Beria, and in 1949-1950 the two engineered the purge and execution of Voznesenskii and other Zhdanov allies in the Leningrad Affair. As this was the first purge of a Politburo member in a decade, it thus marked the beginning of the new crisis. Also in 1949, Molotov, Voroshilov, and Mikoyan were demoted from their ministerial positions; Molotov’s wife was arrested and exiled; and Stalin took to saying that Molotov and Voroshilov had been British spies since 1918. At the same time, another younger contender, Khrushchev, was brought from Kiev to Moscow to counterbalance Malenkov.

zh: 在他的七十寿辰伴随着这类“庆典”之际，显然斯大林正在准备在党内再来一次大规模换岗。但这一次，他的首要目标不是广大干部；他准备攻击的是当年帮他策划大清洗的那批核心近侍。也许他认为助手们已经变得无能，因掌权太久而失去了必不可少的布尔什维克警惕性。也许他转而对付他们，除了老年偏执以及对这些人必定只盼着他死、甚至密谋加速其死亡的恐惧之外，并无别的理由。无论如何，攻击这个制度的核心领导层，比说出怀疑莫洛托夫搞间谍活动更能表明他精神状态的恶化。
en: With such festivities accompanying his seventieth anniversary, it is clear that Stalin was preparing another great changing of the guard within the Party. But this time he was not aiming first at the mass of cadres; he was preparing to attack the nucleus of close aides with which he had engineered the Great Purge. Possibly he believed his assistants had grown ineffective and had lost the requisite Bolshevik vigilance through too long a tenure in power. Possibly he had no reason for turning against them other than senescent paranoia and the fear that they must be living only for his death, or even conspiring to hasten it. In any event, attacking the core leadership of the system was an even greater sign of mental deterioration than voicing suspicions about Molotov’s espionage.

zh: 至于他的近侍们，他们此时认为这种局面不能再持续太久。于是他们敦促他召开一次党代表大会——自1938年以来一次也没有开过——以恢复党章的正常运作。斯大林接受了这个办法，但把它当作发动新一轮清洗的手段。在1952年底的第十九次党代表大会上，他的政策是扩大中央委员会，把政治局（此时改称主席团）的规模扩大一倍，从而把两代元老都淹没在一群只忠于他个人的新人之中。这是把30年代大清洗的手法用于那场清洗的受益者。但此时它是在一个由根深蒂固的干部名录体系所构成的党里施行，这些人若被推翻，必给政权带来灾难；而且它的矛头指向老近卫，这些人不像奥尔忠尼启则或波斯蒂舍夫，他们懂得成熟的斯大林主义机制如何运作，因此可能会设法自保。
en: His close aides, for their part, now believed that this situation could not go on for much longer. They therefore urged him to call a Party Congress—none had met since 1938—in order to reactivate the Party’s constitution. Stalin took them up on this device, but as a means for launching his new purge. At the Nineteenth Party Congress at the end of 1952, his policy was to enlarge the Central Committee and double the size of the Politburo, now renamed Presidium, and thus submerge both generations of the old guard in a group of newcomers beholden to him alone. This was the technique of the Great Purge of the thirties applied to the beneficiaries of that purge. But it was now applied in a Party of entrenched

en: cadres who could not be overturned without bringing disaster to the regime; and it was directed against an old guard whose members, unlike Ordzhonikidze or Postyshev, knew how the mature Stalinist mechanism worked and, therefore, might attempt to defend themselves.

zh: 预定清洗的下一阶段，是1953年1月的医生阴谋案。一批克里姆林宫医生——其中多数人的姓氏是犹太姓氏——因被控谋杀日丹诺夫及犯有其他反苏罪行而被捕。这桩所谓暴行可以像基洛夫遇刺那样，充当借口，用来不断扩大清洗那些为美帝国主义、犹太复国主义效劳并破坏国际共产主义的“叛徒”。而在朝鲜战争和德国即将重新武装所造成的紧张局势下，如此规模的清洗不可避免地会起到——很像1937年清洗所起的作用——为一场重大国际危机、甚至可能是第三次世界大战进行全国心理动员的作用——谁知道呢？
en: The next stage of the intended purge was the Doctors’ Plot of January 1953. A number of Kremlin physicians, most of them with Jewish names, were arrested for the murder of Zhdanov and for other anti-Soviet crimes. Here was the atrocity that could serve, as had Kirov’s murder, as the pretext for an ever-widening purge of “traitors” working for American imperialism, Zionism, and the destruction of international Communism. And a purge of this scope, in the tense situation created by the Korean War and the impending rearmament of Germany, would inevitably have the function—much like that of the purge of 1937—of national psychological mobilization for a major international crisis, even possibly a Third World War—who knows?

zh: 在这场歇斯底里而危险的局面中，斯大林中风了，并于3月5日去世。他可能是被惊恐的随从“送了一程”。也可能是他的身心在这一新事业的紧张压力下垮掉了——他当时73岁。无论如何，他的继承人们立即恢复自己原来的政治局职位，从而废除了十九大的决定，并宣布医生阴谋案是秘密警察捏造的。斯大林时代就这样结束了，而它的事业正要被斯大林本人拆掉。
en: In the midst of this hysterical and dangerous situation, Stalin had a stroke, and on March 5 he died. He could have been assisted on his way by a frightened entourage. Or his physical and mental health could have given way—he was 73 years old—tinder the strain of this new enterprise. In any event, his heirs immediately annulled the decisions of the Nineteenth Congress by resuming their old Politburo positions, and they declared the Doctors’ Plot a police fabrication. The Stalin era thus ended as its work was about to be undetermined by Stalin himself.

zh: 苏联历史的中心篇章就这样结束了。斯大林去世时，距他首次以“乌拉尔—西伯利亚方法”开始改造俄国，正好二十五年。除毛泽东外，他是20世纪主要领导人中在位最久的一位。斯大林的权力运用也是所有领导人（包括毛泽东）中影响最为重大的，因为斯大林创造了共产主义社会的模式，其他共产党领导人或加以模仿，或偶尔试图纠正。相比之下，列宁对俄国和世界的影响都明显较弱。因为列宁的革命虽然创建了党，并在战时共产主义中勾画了新社会的第一个版本，却在1921年不得不放弃其国际抱负和国内社会主义，以失败告终。而如果温和的新经济政策像布哈林所希望的那样延续下去，俄国充其量也只会陷入一种低增长的准社会民主主义而停滞不前——那不会成为任何人的榜样，也不可能奢望扮演重要的国际角色。正是斯大林的自上而下的革命创造了一个激进的新模式，并使制度朝向建设国际强权的方向。因此，正是通过斯大林的行动，列宁那场失败了的革命才得以复活，并扩展到地球的三分之一。
en: So ended the central episode of Soviet history. Stalin died exactly twenty-five years after he had first started to remold Russia by launching the Urals-Siberian method. His was the longest tenure in office of any major twentieth-century leader except Mao Zedong. Stalin’s was also the most momentous exercise of power of any leader, including Mao, because Stalin created the model of Communist society that other Communist leaders imitated or, on occasion, tried to correct. Lenin’s impact, both on Russia and on the world, was by comparison significantly weaker. For Lenin’s Revolution, although it created the Party and sketched the first version of the new society in War Communism, ended in failure when it had to abandon both its international ambitions and its internal socialism in 1921. And if the moderate NEP had continued as Bukharin wished, at best Russia would have bogged down in a slow-growth quasi Social Democracy that would have been a model to no one, and that could not have aspired to a major international role. It was Stalin’s revolution from above that created a radical new model and oriented the system towards building international power. Thus it was through Stalin’s action that Lenin’s failed Revolution was revived and projected across a third of the planet.

zh: 由此产生的斯大林主义制度并不是列宁本人明确设想过的制度，更不是马克思预见过的制度，但这并不使该制度减少一丝一毫的马克思列宁主义性质。意识形态不是蓝图，信徒不能逐条照搬，然后让我们干脆判定某个制度是背叛还是实现了其源头。意识形态是世界观，它把政治行为导向总体目标，并为之划定宽泛的范围。就马克思主义而言，目标是“社会主义”——意即非资本主义——而参数则是历史通过“阶级斗争”无可阻挡地走向这一目标，这场斗争由被剥削的普遍阶级对其“资产阶级”剥削者进行。列宁主义接受了这一切，并增添了一项限定：历史将通过代表无产阶级的党的专政来实现其社会主义目的。
en: That the resulting Stalinist system was not one that Lenin himself had explicitly envisioned, or, even more, one that Marx had anticipated, does not make that system any less Marxist-Leninist. Ideologies are not blueprints that adherents can apply point by point so that we can then say neatly that a given system has betrayed or fulfilled its origins. Ideologies are worldviews that orient political conduct towards general goals and within broad parameters. In the case of Marxism, the goal was “socialism”—in the sense of noncapitalism—and the parameters were history’s inexorable progression towards this goal through the “class struggle” waged by the universal class of the exploited against its “bourgeois” exploiters. Leninism accepted all of this and added to it the parameter that history would realize its socialist purpose through the dictatorship of the Party standing in for the proletariat.

zh: 此外，意识形态如同一切人类目的，都受黑格尔“理性的狡计”支配；也就是说，一切人类行动都不可避免地服务于行动者自己并未意识到的目的。理解斯大林的最好方式，就是把他看作这种反常过程的载体：他以野蛮的方式，借助列宁的党这一工具，建立起马克思的社会主义。然而结果是既可怖又荒诞，并不意味着斯大林背叛了马克思或列宁。它毋宁是说：马克思列宁主义事业本身就不可能实现；因此任何实现它的尝试都必然建立在大量使用暴力的基础上；而这种暴力只能制造出一种荒诞绝伦的超现实。这正是关于苏维埃主义的一大批苏联讽刺文学的意义所在——从1920年叶夫根尼·扎米亚京的《我们》，经1934年安德烈·普拉东诺夫的《基坑》，直到1974年亚历山大·季诺维耶夫的《裂开的高地》。而这确实就是推动整个苏联冒险的“非理性的狡计”。
en: Ideologies, moreover, like all human purposes, are subject to Hegel’s Cunning of Reason; that is, all human actions inevitably serve ends of which the actors themselves are not aware. Stalin is best understood as the vehicle of such a perverse process in the barbarous way he built Marx’s socialism through the instrumentality of Lenin’s Party. Yet that the result was both monstrous and absurd does not mean that Stalin betrayed either Marx or Lenin. It means, rather, that the Marxist-Leninist enterprise was inherently impossible; that any attempt to realize it would therefore have to rest on the massive application of force; and that such an application could only produce a preposterous surreality. This is the meaning of a whole body of Soviet satirical literature about Sovietism, from Evgenii Zamiatin’s

zh: 换一种说法：马克思关于完整社会主义的乌托邦，绝不可能自动从历史逻辑中产生，因此必须由列宁主义的党来强迫历史。没有列宁主义的夺权，资本主义不会在任何地方被消灭，第二国际的马克思主义会在各个福利国家中枯萎消失。证据就在于第二次世界大战后整个欧洲实际发生的事情：非共产主义的马克思主义无一例外地在巴特戈德斯贝格上演了卡诺莎之行。同样，没有斯大林主义自上而下的革命，列宁主义永远不会实现完整社会主义，而只会在一种准市场的、“小资产阶级”的新经济政策中逐渐消磨殆尽。简而言之，实现马克思主义目的的唯一现实途径是列宁主义；而完成列宁主义工程的唯一现实途径是斯大林主义。
en: To put the matter another way, Marx’s Utopia of integral socialism could never result automatically from the logic of history, and so history had to be forced by the Leninist Party. Without the Leninist seizure of power, capitalism would have been suppressed nowhere, and the Second International Marxism would have withered away in a succession of welfare states. The proof of this lies in what actually happened throughout Europe after the Second World War: non-Communist Marxism invariably went to Canossa at Bad Godesberg. Similarly, without the Stalinist revolution from above, Leninism would never have achieved integral socialism, but instead would have dwindled away in a quasi-market, “petty bourgeois” NEP. In short, the only practical way to realize the Marxist purpose was through Leninism; and the only practical way to complete the Leninist project was through Stalinism.

zh: 这条道路之外的另一种选择，是放弃马克思主义社会主义的整个梦想。但鉴于20世纪对完整社会主义的强大推动力，在人们尚未于某处尝试实现这个梦想之前，它被放弃的可能性微乎其微。俄国的坏运气在于，这个梦想最先是在她那里试验的。而她的极大坏运气在于，它竟然是由斯大林这样一个坏透了的人实际贯彻到底的；这一不幸又因他的长寿而加重。因为在斯大林主义制度统治二十五年之后，俄国以及其他所有共产主义体制都已深深地被“谎言”所奴役，以至于它们又花了四十年才找到一条出路。
en: The alternative to this road was to abandon the whole dream of Marxist socialism. But given the overwhelming drive towards integral socialism in the twentieth century, there was little chance that the dream would be abandoned before men had first tried to realize it somewhere. It was Russia’s bad luck that it was tried out there first. And it was her supreme bad luck that it was actually carried through by so bad a man as Stalin, a misfortune that was compounded by his longevity. For after twenty-five years of the Stalinist regime, Russia and all of the other Communist systems were so deeply enthralled to the Lie that it would take them another four decades to find a way out.
